title: Fermi–Dirac occupation in sodium
caption: For n = 2.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³, E_F = (ħ²/2m)(3π²n)^{2/3} = 5.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ J = 3.1 eV. At 300 K, k_BT is only 0.026 eV, so f(E) = 1/(e^{(E−E_F)/k_BT} + 1) is almost a step: states below E_F are full, those above are empty, and only a sliver of width about a few k_BT, under 1% of E_F, is blurred.
alt: Graph of occupation probability against energy: nearly a step from 1 to 0 at the Fermi energy of 3.1 eV, passing through 0.5 there.
description: The horizontal axis is energy in eV; the vertical axis is the occupation probability f(E).
E_F = 3.1 eV is found from the electron density of sodium.
The curve falls from 1 to 0 across a width of order k_BT = 0.026 eV and equals exactly 0.5 at E = E_F.

checks.name: f = ½ at E = E_F = 3.1 eV
states 0.2 eV below E_F are full
